stumbles.quote: 42 of 43 violations with the directive in any form, or with none

stumbles.quote: Naming the forbidden word raised its log-odds by about 2.5.
stumbles.why: It doesn't say which word is forbidden or what task it applies to. It also doesn't say whether 'naming' means putting the word in the prompt. The log-odds of what, and relative to what baseline, is unstated.
The name is never explained. A reader can only guess it is a small language model, and 321M presumably means parameters.

stumbles.quote: Of 22,100 training documents, one has a caps instruction: 'NEVER give a baby honey'.
stumbles.why: The link to the earlier findings is implied but not stated, presumably that caps emphasis is nearly absent from the training data. The corpus isn't identified either.

point: A tiny 321M model ignored all-caps instructions, and even mentioning the forbidden word made it more likely to say it. The likely reason is that its training corpus almost never contains caps-emphasized instructions.
